lesson.label: The Lesson
lesson.text:
Hello! Today we are learning about families. This lesson is called "What can families teach us?" You will draw your family, say their names, and think about what they teach you. By the end, you will be able to tell someone all about your family. You need paper, crayons, and your talking voice. A grown-up can sit with you. There are six little steps. Here comes step one! Step 1: Who is in my family? Think about the people you live with. Draw them all on your paper. Then count how many people you drew, and say the number out loud. A good job looks like this: every person in your home is on the paper, even the little ones. It does not have to be neat! 😊

Tell me when you are done.

overview.label: Unit Overview
overview.text:
Hello! Today we start Unit 1. It is called "What can families teach us?"

In this unit we talk about the people in your family. We draw them, we say their names, and we find out what they teach us. At the end, you will make a big My Family poster. We do this because your family is special, and talking about people you love helps you learn to talk, listen and find things out. You will need paper, crayons, and a grown-up sitting with you. There are six little steps, and we do one at a time. I will always wait for you. Here comes step one: Who is in my family? Look around your home. Think about the people you live with. Tell me their names out loud, and count them on your fingers. A good answer sounds like this: "In my family there is my Hooyo, my Aabo and me. That is three people."

Now you try. Who is in your family? 🙂

goals.label: My Learning Goals
goals.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this page is our map. 🗺️

This page shows our learning goals. Goals are the things you will be able to do by the end of Unit 1. Our big question is: What can families teach us? We look at the goals first so you know where we are going. You will need your voice, and a grown-up nearby to help you read. There are 3 little steps. Here comes step one! Step 1: Listen to our goals. I will say them, and you say "yes" after each one you like the sound of. We will learn who is in your family. We will learn what you call them, like Hooyo or Ayeeyo. We will learn what your family does together. We will learn what your family teaches you. We will say thank you. We will ask an older person a question. Now tell me: which one sounds the most fun to you?

project.label: Mini-Project
project.text:
Hello! Today we are making your My Family poster. 🎨

It is a big picture of the people you love, all on one paper. We do it so you can show someone your family and talk about them. There are five steps. We will do one at a time. You will need a big paper, crayons or pencils, and your grown-up nearby. Here comes step one! Step 1: Draw the people you love. In the middle of your paper, draw everyone who lives with you. You can add Ayeeyo, Awoowe, or a pet too. Give everyone a big smile! Take your time — there's no rush. Tell me when you are done.

reflect.label: Reflection
reflect.text:
Hello! This page is called Reflection. That means we look back and think about our learning. You have done lots of lovely work about your family. Now you get to say what you liked best and who you want to thank. This helps you remember it, and it is a real Global Perspectives skill. You just need your voice, and a grown-up nearby if you like. There are three little steps. Here comes step one. Finish this out loud, then type it to me: "The thing I like best about my family is ..."

A good answer says one thing, not lots. Like "they make me laugh" or "we eat together". Take your time — there's no rush.

teacher.label: Teacher Session
teacher.text:
Hello! Let's get ready for your teacher session together. 😊

In the teacher session, you sit with other children and you talk about your family, and you listen to them talk about theirs. That is a big Global Perspectives skill: talking and listening. Today I will help you practise, so when it is your turn you feel brave and ready. You just need your voice, and a grown-up sitting near you. There are four small steps. Here comes step one. Step one: tell me who is in your family. Say each person out loud, then count them. A good answer names every person you live with, like "my mum, my dad, my brother — that is three."

Take your time — there's no rush.

overview.label: Unit Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 2. Our big question is: What kind of garden would be best? In this unit we will look at gardens, find out what plants need, and plant a seed or draw our own garden. We do it to grow three skills: looking closely, saying why you like something, and finding things out. What I expect from you: talk out loud, point at things, and try your best. There are no marks here. Have a pencil and paper near you, and a grown-up if one is close by. There are 3 small steps on this page. Here comes step one. Step one: close your eyes and think of a garden you have seen. Then tell me one thing that was in it.

lesson.label: The Lesson
lesson.text:
Hello! Today we are doing our garden lesson. 🌱

This lesson is all about gardens. We will look at a garden, draw one, and find out what plants need to grow. By the end, you will be able to tell someone what a plant needs to grow big. You will need your eyes, your voice, and a pencil and paper for drawing. A grown-up can sit with you too. There are six parts, and I will give you one at a time. Here comes part one: Look at the garden. Go and look at a garden with your grown-up. It can be a real garden outside, or a picture of a garden in a book. Then tell me one thing you can see. I am hoping you can spot things like a plant, a flower, some soil, a tree, or maybe a butterfly! Take your time — there's no rush.

bigideas.label: Big Ideas
bigideas.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this page is called "Look after your seed."

This is about caring for the seed you planted in a cup. We do it because a seed is a living thing, and it needs our help to wake up and grow. By the end, you will know how to look after your plant every day, and you will draw it. You will need your seed cup, a little water, and a pencil or crayons. A grown-up can sit with you. There are 5 small steps. Here comes step one! Step 1: Tell me the three things your plant needs to grow. Say them out loud, then type them for me. I am hoping for three words. Take your time — there's no rush.

project.label: Mini-Project
project.text:
Welcome to your Mini-Project! This is the big fun part of our garden unit. 🌱

You will do one of two things: plant a real seed in a cup, or draw your best garden. You can do both if you want! By the end, you will show your plant or your picture to someone and tell them about it. Here is what I expect from you: try your best, be gentle with your plant, and use your words to tell me what you did. There are 4 steps. I will give you one at a time. You will need a grown-up nearby, and either a cup with soil and a seed, or paper and crayons. Step 1: Choose your project. Do you want to plant a seed, or draw your best garden? Tell me which one you pick, and one reason why. A good answer sounds like: "I pick the drawing, because I love flowers."

goals.label: My Learning Goals
goals.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this page is called My Learning Goals. Learning goals are the things you will be able to do by the end of our garden unit. We look at them first so you know where we are going, like looking at a map before a walk. By the end of this activity, you will know your goals and which one is new for you. You need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up nearby. There are 4 small steps. Here comes step one. Step one: look at your goals on the page and read them out loud with your grown-up. There are five. They are about looking at a garden, naming a plant, knowing what a plant needs, planting or drawing a garden, and telling someone about it. A good job here is saying each one slowly and pointing to it with your finger. Tell me when you have read them all. 🌱

reflect.label: Reflection
reflect.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this page is our look-back. Look-back means we stop and think about our garden project. We remember what we did, and we say what we liked best. This is real Global Perspectives work — good thinkers always look back. By the end, you will be able to tell someone what you learned and what you enjoyed. You need your voice, and a grown-up sitting near you. A pencil too, if you want to draw. There are four steps. Here comes step one. Step one: tell me what you made in this project. Did you plant a seed in a cup, or did you draw your best garden? Or both? A good answer tells me one thing about it. Like "I planted a bean seed" or "I drew sunflowers and a bench". Take your time — there's no rush. Tell me when you are ready.

teacher.label: Teacher Session
teacher.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this is our garden session for Unit 2. We are going to find out what makes a garden good. You will look, talk, choose, and say why — those are big Global Perspectives skills. By the end, you will be able to name what a plant needs and say which garden you like best. You need your eyes, your voice, and maybe a pencil and paper. A grown-up nearby can help. We have 5 steps. Step 1: Look at a garden. It can be a real garden outside, or a picture in a book, or one you remember. Tell me two things you can see in it. A good answer names real things, like "a green plant" or "brown soil". Off you go — I'm listening. 🌱

lesson.label: The Lesson
lesson.text:
Hello! Today we are learning about jobs. A job is the work a person does. We will look at people at work, see how they help us, and find out what they use. By the end, you will be able to name lots of jobs and say how one person helps us. You will need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up next to you. A pencil and paper too, if you have one. There are six little steps. I will give you one at a time. Step one: Jobs I can see. Look at the pictures on your page. Point to each person and say the job out loud, in a big voice. Try to find these: a teacher, a doctor, a farmer, a driver, a market seller, a builder. Tick a box each time you name one. A good job here means you SAY the word out loud, not just point. 🙂

Tell me when you are done, and tell me one job you saw.

overview.label: Unit Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this is Unit 3: What do we know about jobs? In this unit we find out about the jobs people do. A job is the work a person does. We will name jobs, meet the people who help us, look at the tools they use, and draw the job YOU would like to do one day. Why do we do this? Because jobs are all around you, and looking closely at the world is a big Global Perspectives skill. What I expect from you: talk to me, point at things, and try even when you are not sure. There are no marks here. A grown-up can sit with you and read with you. We have three small steps on this page. Here comes step one. Step one: look around the room you are in, or think about your street. Tell me one person you have seen working. What were they doing?

goals.label: My Learning Goals
goals.text:
Hello! Today we are looking at your Learning Goals for Unit 3, "What do we know about jobs?"

Learning goals are the things you will be able to do by the end of this unit. We look at them first so you know where we are going. By the end of this chat, you will know which goals feel easy and which ones we still need to practise. You need your voice, and a grown-up nearby to help you read and tick. That's all! There are four goals. I will read you one at a time. For each one, tell me "yes I can", or "not yet". Both answers are great — "not yet" just means we practise together. Here comes goal one. I can name some jobs people do. Can you name one job right now? Say it out loud, then tell me. 🙂

project.label: Mini-Project
project.text: Hello! Today we are doing your Mini-Project for Unit 3. That means you will draw the job YOU would like to do when you grow up, and then show it and talk about it. We do this because it helps you notice all the jobs people do, and it helps you speak proudly about your own idea. By the end, you will have a picture and you will be able to tell someone what you would do and what you would use. You will need paper and crayons or coloured pencils, and a grown-up sitting with you. Here is what I expect from you: pick one job you really like, think before you draw, use lots of colour, and use your big proud voice at the end. There are no wrong dreams. Any job you like is a good one. There are 6 steps. Let's start with something small. Step 1: Close your eyes and think. What job would you like to do when you grow up? A doctor? A farmer? A teacher? A fisher? A pilot? Pick just one — the one you like best. Tell me the job you chose. 🙂

reflect.label: Reflection
reflect.text:
Welcome to our Reflection! This is the last part of our jobs unit. Reflection means looking back and saying what you learned and what you liked. We do it because your thinking matters just as much as your drawing. By the end, you will be able to say the job you would like and the part you liked best. You just need your voice, and your grown-up nearby to help. There are 2 small steps. Step 1: Finish this sentence out loud, then type it to me. "The job I would like to do is ..."

A good answer names one job, like doctor, farmer, fisher, teacher or pilot. Take your time — there's no rush. 🙂

teacher.label: Teacher Session
teacher.text:
Hello! I'm Wehel Tutor, and today I'm your teacher for our Teacher Session on jobs. 🙂

In a teacher session we play, we talk, and we share. This one is about the jobs people do — like a teacher, a farmer or a fisher. By the end you will be able to name some jobs, say how one person helps us, and tell me the job you would like to do. What you need: your voice, your grown-up sitting with you, and space to wave your arms for acting. Before we start, three little rules: there are no wrong dreams, a girl can be anything and a boy can be anything, and we take turns and listen. There are 4 steps. Here comes step one. Step 1: The naming game. Tell me as many jobs as you can think of. A good answer is three or more jobs, said out loud. I will start you off with one: teacher. Your turn — what jobs can you name?

lesson.label: The Lesson
lesson.text:
Hello! Today's lesson is called "How can we save water?"

We will look at water together. You will find out where we use water, why water is so special, and how you can save it. There are six little parts. I will give you one at a time. All you need is your eyes, your voice, and maybe a pencil. A grown-up can sit with you too. Here comes part one! Part 1 is "Where do we use water?" Look at the list on your page. It says drinking, washing hands, brushing teeth, cooking, watering plants, and giving water to animals. Tick the ones you do at home. Then count your ticks and tell me the number. 💧

goals.label: My Learning Goals
goals.text:
Hello! I am your teacher today. 🌊

This page is called My Learning Goals. It shows the four things you will be able to do in this water unit. We look at them so you know what you are aiming for, and so you can feel proud when you can do them. I expect you to say each goal out loud with me, then tell me if you can do it yet. A good answer is a real answer — "yes I can" or "not yet". Both are great! There are four goals. Here comes goal one. Goal one: I can name a way we use water. Say one way you use water at home. Take your time — there's no rush.

overview.label: Unit Overview
overview.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher, and we are starting Unit 4: How can we save water? This first page is our "meet and get ready" page. We meet Zane, a boy at Ehel Academy in Hargeisa who loves water. By the end of this page you will be able to say how YOU use water, and you will know what we will learn in this unit. You just need your voice, and a grown-up nearby if you like. There are 3 small steps. Here comes step one. Step 1: Think about today. Tell me one time you used water today. It could be a drink, washing your hands, or brushing your teeth. A good answer is one clear thing, in a full sentence, like "I used water to wash my hands."

Your turn — tell me one way you used water today.

bigideas.label: Big Ideas
bigideas.text:
Hello! Today we are looking at the Big Ideas of our water unit. These are the two most important things to remember: every drip of water counts, and we can make a water promise. We do this so you can look after water at home, all by yourself. By the end, you will be able to count drips, check a tap, and say a promise out loud. You will need your voice, your fingers for counting, and a grown-up nearby. There are four small steps. Here comes step one. Look at the water drops on your page: 💧 💧 💧 💧 💧

Count them out loud, slowly. Then hold up that many fingers and tell me the number.

project.label: Mini-Project
project.text:
Welcome to your big water project! 💧

This is the last part of Unit 4. You will make a water-saving poster, or say a water promise, and share it with your family or class. We do this so you can show what you know: water is precious, and even you can help save it. By the end, you will have one bright poster with words on it, and you will say your promise out loud. You need paper, crayons or coloured pencils, and a grown-up sitting with you. There are five steps. Here comes step one. Step 1: Choose your best idea. Think of ONE way you can save water. Here are some ideas to help you:
turn the tap off while you brush your teeth
tell a grown-up about a dripping tap
catch the rain in a bucket for the plants
give the washing water to the plants
have a quick wash, not a long one

A good answer is one idea, said out loud to your grown-up, in a full sentence like "I can save water by..."

Now tell me: which idea did you choose?

teacher.label: Teacher Session
teacher.text: Welcome to our Teacher Session! 💧 This is our talking and playing lesson about water. We will look, talk, play a game, and say a water chant together. By the end, you will be able to say how we use water, why water is precious, and one way to save it. You need your voice, your hands, and a grown-up sitting near you. There are 5 steps. Here comes step one. Step one: our water walk. Walk around your home with your grown-up. Point at every place where we use water — the tap, the kitchen, the washing, the plants, the animals. Count the places out loud. A good job looks like this: you point, you say the place, and you tell me your number at the end. Zane found six places! Off you go — tell me your number when you come back.

reflect.label: Reflection
reflect.text:
Hello! Today we are doing the Reflection page — that means looking back at your water project and feeling proud. 💧

We do this because good thinkers always look back and think: what did I learn? Grown-up scientists do this too! By the end you will be able to say what you learned about water, and how you helped. You will need your Reflection sheet, a pencil, some crayons, and a grown-up sitting beside you. There are three steps. Here comes step one. Step 1: Look at the list of things you did. Read each line out loud with your grown-up. Then tick a happy face if you did it, or a straight face if it is not quite there yet. What I expect from you: be honest. A straight face is not bad! It just means "not yet". Honest ticking is the best kind of ticking. Tell me when you have ticked them all.
